projects.description:
Refugees come to Montenegro with a variety skills, knowledge, expertise and assets. As much has 40% of adult refugees have university diploma. Among holders of temporary protection, there are over 80% of university graduates or above. Some 16% of refugees set up their business in Montenegro (with 67% of entrepreneurs being women) with much more that are interested in it. 
In 2024, the UNHCR worked with refugee communities to unlock their potential by creating various opportunities and support channels. Thanks to the profiling of the population that UNHCR has been taking throughout the year, reliable, up-to-date,  and accurate information were made possible. They have provided a basis for effective advocacy, both for individual cases and at the systemic level.
Through diversified partnerships, steps were taken to ensure the unhindered recognition of diplomas, provide grant opportunities, and increase employment prospects. More efforts will be made in 2024 to ensure that refugees' voices directly shape the short-term and mid-term strategic orientation of the UNHCR office, enabling the full utilization of the capacities of displaced and stateless populations.

projects.name: E-Social: Leveraging Digital Solutions to Enable Efficient Social Protection of the Vulnerable
projects.description:
UNDP has supported the Government of Montenegro in establishing the national Integrated Social Welfare Information System (e-Social IS), which has been in operation since January 2015. Being the backbone of the country's social protection system, e-Social is in charge of processing nearly all social protection entitlements. 

To provide timely and efficiently cash transfers and social services and to ensure that new legislative solutions are duly enforced, it is necessary to continuously invest in the e-Social IS. To that end, the project envisages key components, including the development of new and upgraded functionalities (including its e-services for citizens), IS refactoring, capacity-building support for IS administrators and end-users, as well as its maintenance to ensure medium-term sustainability. The project will also provide, until 31 December 2027, procurement of additional server capacities as well as regular hardware supply replacement and maintenance in 36 remote locations.

projects.description: The Administrative Court of Montenegro is the 2nd instance institution in the asylum procedures and the 3rd instance institution in the statelessness determination procedure. Work with asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness pose different challenges to the court: from interpretation services, to more specific knowledge on different topics (country of origin information, unaccompanied and separated children, family reunification cases, credibility assessment, etc.). During 2023-2025, UNHCR organized several workshops for judges of the Administrative Court and the Bar Association, to facilitate discussion on several asylum related topics. The Ombudsperson is the main national human rights institution whose role in access to territory and detention facilities is of utmost importance for asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness. In 2024, UNHCR and the Ombudsperson renewed Memorandum of Understanding to define cooperation in the area of joint interest, such as border monitoring.

projects.name: Technical and expert support to the Ministry of Justice to secure access to state funded free legal aid scheme for vulnerable persons and group of persons
projects.description: As per the 2011 Law on Free Legal Aid, state funded free legal aid covers a number of court procedures for socially vulnerable persons, but it does not cover judicial procedure for determination of date and place of birth of persons born at home, as well as all administrative procedures, including refugee status determination procedure and statelessness determination procedure. Refugees and persons missing birth registration are among the most vulnerable groups of persons in Montenegro, who often does not speak Montenegrin language and live on margins of society. Due to that reason, the Law on Free Legal Aid needs to be amended to introduce above mentioned specific procedures in the state funded free legal aid scheme. In addition, a tailor made information material needs to be produced to introduce these categories of persons with the benefits and possibilities of the state funded free legal aid scheme in procedures that they need to initiate. On that way Montenegro will implement recommendations of the UN Committee against torture, issued in the 2022 report on Montenegro. In 2025, the UN Human Rights Committee recommended to Montenegro to amend the Law on Free Legal Aid to introduce birth registration, statelessness determination and refugee status determination procedures in the state funded free legal aid system. Also, the Law should be amended to enable state funding to NGOs registered for provision of free legal aid.
projects.outcome: 4.1. Rule of law and justice for all

projects.description:
In 2024/25, UNHCR sustained its efforts to facilitate labor market access for asylum seekers. A significant advocacy focus was on reducing the waiting period for asylum seekers to gain employment rights from nine months post-application. The authorities have acknowledged the validity of this proposal, and it is anticipated that the legislative framework will be amended accordingly in 2026.
UNHCR also intensified its collaboration with the Employment Agency, resulting in the creation of joint informational materials to be disseminated to all individuals under UNHCR's mandate, thereby enhancing their awareness of employment process and opportunities. Additionally, UNHCR addressed fundamental issues such as the recognition of foreign diplomas in partnership with the Ministry of Education and funded small-scale language learning initiatives.

projects.name: Support refugees' entrepreneurial pursuits through the promotion of thier economic and financial inclusion
projects.description:
A proportionally large number of persons with international and temporary protection in Montenegro are interested in establishing their businesses. This is why UNHCR intensified its efforts to ensure support for their entrepreneurial pursuits.
Namely, in 2024 UNHCR established communication with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), resulting in their willingness to apply  support program for Ukrainian refugees to Montenegro. This program, which is currently available in only a few European countries,  provides refugee entrepreneurs with grants of up to 10,000 EUR to cover business consultancy needs. Additionally, refugees will benefit from upskilling and reskilling training, as well as language courses, that started on the 2nd half of 2025. Together with the EBRD, UNHCR organised a workshop to present these opportunities to beneficiaries.
Further on, UNHCR continued advancing financial inclusion through  fostering cooperation with the Central Bank of Montenegro. That resulted in the establishment of clear appeal procedures for refugees whose access to bank accounts may have been denied. Additionally, in cooperation with the Central Bank, UNHCR produced informational materials detailing the bank account opening procedure. Direct cooperation with commercial banks and the association of business banks to ensure refugees can access the full spectrum of financial services was also inititated.

projects.name: Prevent and combat manifestations of racism, racial discrimination, violence, xenophobia and related intolerance against all refugees and promote an open and evidence-based public dialog on the position of refugees in Montenegro.
projects.description:
In 2024, the UNHCR collaborated with both refugee and host communities to prevent instances of racial, national, and other forms of discrimination. Through a series of outreach events with refugee communities, the UNHCR gained a comprehensive understanding of the dynamics between refugees and the host community.
To foster closer relations, the UNHCR organized various sports, leisure, and educational activities, most notably in cooperation with the Football Association of Montenegro and the Olympic Committee. The inclusion of refugees in sports activities proved to be an effective means of promoting their broader socio-economic integration.
Additionally, the UNHCR produced a series of successful web stories featuring refugees and stateless individuals. These stories, made available to the public, highlighted the resilience, strength, and capabilities of the populations under the UNHCR's mandate.

projects.name: Support the national authorities in creating inclusive and equitable quality education for refugees and stateless children and youth at all levels.
projects.description: In 2024, UNHCR worked to support the education of refugee children, with the focus on increasing the primary school enrolment rate for Ukrainian refugees and the provision of support in overcoming language, cultural, psychological and other obstacle to equitable and quality education, to result in a better learning outcome for refuge children. As a result of the serial of workshops with refugee parents, which were coordinated by the Ministry of Education, Innovation and Science, the primary school enrollment rate of Ukrainian refuges increased. In addition, as a result of the improved cooperation on with the Ministry and upon the UNHCR’s advocacy efforts,  the Law on General Education was amended to include stateless persons and to ensure adequate support to refugee children. The need for a specific support to refuge children was also acknowledged in the Strategy of Education to cover the period up until 2030, which was enabled in cooperation with UNICEF.

projects.name: Facilitate the certificate recognition for refugees to ensure that their prior learning was recognized and valorized in education and employment
projects.description:
Following UNHCR's advocacy efforts, the Ministry of Education, Science, and Innovation prepared amendments to the Law on Recognition of Foreign Diplomas and Qualifications, adopted by the Parliament in 2025. These amendments are opening possibility for adoption of by-law to the amended Law, to secure that refugees cannot always obtain all the documents necessary for the recognition of foreign diplomas as required by regular procedures. During 2026, UNHCR expects to work with the education ministry on the above mentioned by-law.
Consequently, the Ministry of Education has started collaborating with the Council of Europe to determine the manner of establishing qualifications and skills for refugees who do not possess the respective educational certificates (prior test). UNHCR will continue to make significant effort to contribute to the adoption of this procedure.

projects.name: Support the national system to ensure that refugee children residing in Montenegro and particularly those who are born in Montenegro, can enjoy the full scope of services aimed at attaining the highest level of early childhood development, successfully overcoming language, cultural and social barriers
projects.description:
In 2025, UNHCR continued its efforts to ensure that early childhood development and education services are accessible to displaced and stateless children. Particular attention was given to ensuring that legal status does not pose an obstacle to early childhood development. In this regard, UNHCR and the Ministry of Interior prepared a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to ensure that children born on the territory of Montenegro can acquire Montenegrin citizenship. Access to citizenship is expected to help these children obtain the services necessary for early childhood development.
*While this part of the initiative has been completed, the monitoring of the SOP's implementation and other related activities will be incorporated into the sub-output addressing adequate and timely access to quality services that meet the needs of all men, women, girls, and boys.ID: 111796

projects.name: Support Ministry of the Interior to amend the Law on Foreigners, and harmonize other legislation accordingly
projects.description: In 2022 Montenegro started to amend its Law on Foreigners to strengthen the statelessness determination procedure, as well as other issues relevant for persons of concern to UNHCR, such as: issuing of visas for a person in family reunification procedure; access to labor market for persons granted international protection; etc. In addition, number of laws needs to be harmonized with the Law on Foreigners, to recognize stateless persons as beneficiaries of that law, thus creating condition for effective access to rights for persons granted stateless status. The draft amendments to the law has been prepared by the MoI, through cooperation with UNHCR. The draft Law is expected to be adopted in early 2026.

In 2023, the MoI, in cooperation with UNHCR, adopted Operational guidelines for birth registration, to be used by the MoI, elementary school, municipal centers for social care and health care centers when dealing with children missing birth registration. In addition, the draft SOP on access to citizenship for children born in Montenegro from the unknown parents, or whose parents are without citizenship, or who will otherwise be stateless, are prepared and should be adopted in early 2024.

projects.name: Support line institutions to improve the standards in access to territory and asylum procedure in line with the UNHCR's and Montenegrin Ombudsman's findings from the 2022/23 partnership projects
projects.description: While Montenegro is a positive example in the region in relation to access to territory, the Ombudsman/UNHCR projects implemented in 2022 and 2023 provided clear indicators on where the focus should be put in the following period. As the outcome, the Border Police of Montenegro and UNHCR posted a 6-languages poster (Montenegrin, English, Arabic, Farsi, Russian and Spanish) in all sea/land/air border crossings, with information to interested persons on possibility to apply for asylum in Montenegro. The poster contains QR code that leads to UNHCR hotline and HELP page, containing additional information on asylum system of Montenegro and assistance that a person can get if s/he decides to apply for asylum. In addition, the Border Police opened possibility for registration of asylum intention in all police stations in Montenegro, in line with the 2018 asylum law. Other Ombudsman's recommendations, related to capacity building of Border Police, will be included in UNHCR's training and advocacy activities.

Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR)
projects.description: Within the Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR) programme, IOM works with national and international partners in both, the host country and the country of origin, to ensure that beneficiaries willing to return to their countries of origin are able to travel in a safe and dignified manner - from host country to their final destination in country of origin.  Beneficiaries will be supported to return to their country of origin by organizing all travel arrangements including flight bookings, facilitating the issuance of travel documents when required in cooperation with the authorities of origin and/or host countries, carrying out airport clearance and other procedures as necessary, making transit and reception arrangements, facilitating pre-migration health checks, informing migrants of their travel schedules and entitlements (return allowances, luggage allowances). Additionally, upon their return to the country of origin, based on criteria associated with reintegration needs and vulnerability, beneficiaries are provided with tailored reintegration assistance in an individualized, timely and effective manner. Those not provided with reintegration assistance will continue to receive counselling and onward referral where feasible.

projects.description: Better quality of local self-governments services provided to citizens depends on transparent and inclusive planning of local policies, effective and timely execution and transparent and responsible reporting on achieved objectives and results. This could be achieved only with systematic, holistic approach in combining activities for smooth and continued flow of data and information used for evidence-based, immediate decision making and administering of assigned tasks and affairs. Design, purchase and functioning of the unique software for administering local public revenues will set for unified and standardized operating system for all local self-governments in determining, collecting and control of local public revenues. This will form solid basis for better planning and allocation of local public budgets and more effective planning and execution of local policies and achieving strategic objectives. This will allow timely and up-to-date information for open and result-oriented reporting to the local Parliaments and citizens.

projects.description: The objective of this technical assistance is to take the initial steps in introducing land consolidation in Montenegro and implementing land consolidation pilots. The legal review of the draft Law on agricultural land and its subsequent adoption, are prerequisites for the full implementation of the pilot projects. The overall goal is to better align the legal and regulatory framework governing land with the strategic objectives of the Government and enhance the potential of the agricultural sector. The project will also strengthen institutional capacities to manage state land efficiently and to design and implement land consolidation projects.
projects.outcome: 1.1.Private sector growth, economic transformation and decent jobs

projects.name: ITU-EKIP Regulatory Forum for Europe 2023
projects.description: The ITU-EKIP Regional Regulatory Forum for Europe on "Universal Connectivity in Europe: The Current State and Future Prospects", which will be held from 28 to 29 September 2023 in Budva, and co-organized by the ITU Office for Europe and EKIP. This Regional Forum will build upon the outcomes of the Global Symposium for Regulators 2023 and its Best Practice Guidelines. It will provide a unique opportunity for high-level dialogue between stakeholders on strategies and policies directed towards broadband development in the region. In this regard, it will facilitate discussions on the challenges and opportunities offered by resilient high-speed networks coupled with regulatory actions that are flexible and collaborative. This event will also offer an opportunity for setting up actions to assist countries on regulatory matters.  It will cover, in particular, the following aspects: Market and Technological Trends; Future of Regulation in the Digital Era; Consumer information, protection, and rights; Further Steps Towards the Unique EU Market; IPv6 Implementation. The Forum targets explicitly European Regulatory Agencies, Ministries, Operators of Electronic Communications, Academia, and other stakeholders active in the ICT regulatory field.

projects.name: To produce and ensure the full functionality and service continuity of the electronic monitoring system (EMS) related to implementation of restraining order security measure for perpetrators of gender-based violence
projects.description: To produce and ensure the full functionality and service continuity of the electronic monitoring system (EMS) related to implementation of restraining order security measure for perpetrators of gender-based violence. In 2025 the support will be extended to the Ministry of Justice of Montenegro by enhancing both human and technical capacities to implement electronic protection measures- bracelet system (EMS) for both victims and perpetrators of violence. This support will include UN Women Serbia providing expertise and assistance for possible legislative and procedural interventions to fully integrate EMS. Efforts will also focus on trainings and capacity-building for stakeholders involved in preventing and responding to violence against women and domestic violence ( at least 100 representatives of justice, police, health and social sector ) to utilize additional protection measure to increase women safety, fostering their mutual cooperation and collaborating with two selected specialized local civil society organizations, SOS telefon za zene i djecu zrtve nasilja and Women Rights Center Podgorica. Their activities will further broad awareness and empower women victims and those at risk of gender-based violence (at least 100 will be directly reached through workshops, info session, provision of specialized service for victims /witnesses and free legal aid, info materials, street actions and campaign during 16 days of activism against violence against women ) and educate them to use available prevention and protection mechanisms and services, particularly EMS.

projects.name: National workshop on the findings of the application of the equitable access score-card in Montenegro
projects.description: The self-assessment’s findings revealed significant data gaps in assessing access to water and sanitation in rural areas and for vulnerable and marginalized groups. Additionally, fragmented institutional responsibilities and the lack of an inter-ministerial approach were identified. Participants urged the need to develop a detailed action plan to address these challenges and improve equitable access to water and sanitation. This plan would be structured based on the different equity dimensions, namely addressing geographical disparities, ensuring access to vulnerable groups and affordability of water and sanitation services.

projects.name: Technical assistance for Sustainable Forest Management
projects.description: The overall goal of the project is to enhance institutional capacities for the preparation and monitoring of Forest Management Plans in private forests. The project is specifically geared towards enhancing forest management in Montenegro, particularly within private forest areas. Key project activities encompass assessing the current methodology for private forest management plans, evaluating the capacities of the forthcoming state-owned forest management enterprise, and developing policy paper and methodology for the monitoring and management of private forests. Utilizing GIS and GPS technologies for delineation and monitoring, organizing hands-on training to enhance skills, and formulating effective Forest Management Plans are central to the project's goals. Additionally, stakeholder consultations, policy formulation, and knowledge sharing through study tours constitute integral components, fostering sustainable forest management and contributing to Montenegro's environmental and socio-economic development.

projects.name: Establishment of Internet Protocol version 6 Laboratory
projects.description: In September 2023, there will be an opening ceremony of the IPv6 Laboratory which will take place at the University of Montenegro in Podgorica. In 2021, ITU has provided assistance to the Government of Montenegro and the Agency for Electronic Communications and Postal Services of Montenegro (EKIP) for the development of a National Workshop on Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) strategies, policies, and implementation, the organization of a “training of experts" equipping more than 20 professionals in Montenegro on the transition from IPv4 to IPv6, and the elaboration of an ITU Technical Assistance paper detailing the building blocks for future actions needed at the country level including requirements for the elaboration of the IPv6 laboratory, cost estimations and use cases. To support this process, an IPv6 Laboratory was created at country level to provide the foundation for educational programmes in third-level education, and re-skilling and upskilling trainings. This event inaugurates the opening of the IPv6 Laboratory under the framework of ITU Europe Regional Initiative 1 Digital Infrastructure Development.

projects.name: More efficient people-centred public administration
projects.description:
In order to create an environment for efficient communication between citizens and public administration, the Project will build capacities of the Ministry of Public Administration (MPA) as the key institution in coordinating the public administration reform. The Project will focus on two outputs: 
1) standardizing functioning of public institutions, which is a part of the administration lacking normative framework, and upgrading institutional capacities of the MPA, as a coordinating body of public administration reform, reflected in the Output 1 - Increased efficiency through standardized functioning of public administration.
2) standardization of human-centered e-services and further development of digital skills of the citizens and businesses, reflected in the Output 2 - Increased digital efficiency of public administration serving citizens and businesses.

projects.name: Roll-out of HerCyberTracks at the Western Balkan Cyber Capacity Center
projects.description: ITU and the Western Balkans Cyber Capacity Center (WB3C) are strengthening cooperation, by launching the Her CyberTracks Initiative Regional Forum at the Western Balkans Cyber Capacity Center (WB3C) in Podgorica, Montenegro. ITU and GIZ have partnered on the "Her CyberTracks" initiative to build cybersecurity capacities and promote inclusivity. This initiative aims to provide capacity building and training, with a specific focus on women in cybersecurity policymaking and diplomacy. By supporting women in becoming leaders in this field, the Her CyberTracks Initiative seeks to bridge gender, capacity, and workforce gaps in cybersecurity, thus driving positive change. The Forum will be hosted in WB3C and will welcome over 50 women leaders from the targeted countries (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine.).
